name: メモと順序変更を備える保存地点の行
prompt:
Create one Japanese saved-place list row as a standalone, wide mobile UI component on a clean white canvas.

Reference priority:
1) The first image is the original full row crop and controls the image position and crop, typography hierarchy, rating layout, metadata order, note field, and reorder handle.
2) The second image is an exact crop of the original listing photograph. Preserve this photograph and its crop as faithfully as possible: a pale ceramic teapot with a turquoise lid pouring tea into a blue-striped bowl on a stone table. Do not replace it with another photo, redraw its objects, add detail, recolor it, or apply a filter.
3) The third image is the Japanese adaptation preview. Use it for the exact Japanese copy and Lighthouse green only; the original row and photo control the layout and visual details.

Include exactly:
- One square, softly rounded thumbnail at the far left using the original photograph.
- Title “1. 地域の食堂” in near-black Meiryo-style bold text.
- A rating row with exactly four filled rounded-square green tiles, each containing one white star, followed by one neutral-gray fifth star tile; then “4.2” and “(2千件)”.
- An outlined location pin, then “渋谷区・料金の目安 ¥¥¥”.
- The category line “食事・カフェ・麺料理”.
- A wide, softly rounded note field with a very light green-neutral fill and exact placeholder “メモを書く…”.
- A thin, pale-gray three-line reorder handle at the far right, aligned with the row content.
- A subtle pale-gray divider along the bottom edge.

Use #2D8F5E for the four filled rating tiles, white stars, near-black #1D1D1D for the title and rating number, and calm slate #6E6E6E for metadata and placeholder. Use Meiryo-style Japanese sans-serif: title Bold20/28, rating and metadata Regular14/20, placeholder Regular14/20. Keep a compact wide row, align the photo, content, note field, and reorder handle cleanly, and preserve generous legibility without clipping.

Do not add other list rows, a phone frame, navigation, map, extra ratings, extra stars, more text, or a watermark. Keep the supplied photograph visually recognizable and unchanged in subject, color, crop, and visible details.
